title: The surah opens with the sun and its full light.
subtitle: Why the brightest thing in the sky is sworn by

row.title: a pair of opposites
sub: light and dark, good and evil

then: Early Makkah, with opposition to the Prophet ﷺ growing hard. The surah starts with a run of oaths, and the first is {reward}the sun and its light{/reward}. Mujahid said it means its light; Qatadah said the whole day. {idea}The oaths build toward one point about the human soul.{/idea}
now: Morning light comes through the blinds and you reach for your phone before you notice it. Ten minutes of headlines, then the commute. {idea}The light was a message before it was a weather report.{/idea} It is the opening line of an argument about you.
old: Sunlight is just the start of another busy day.
new: The sun is sworn by because something just as clear is about to be said about me.
try: Tomorrow, before you check your phone, look at the morning light for ten seconds.

title: The moon follows the sun and borrows its place.
subtitle: Something that comes after, in order
then: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas said the moon {idea}follows the sun{/idea}, or follows the day. Qatadah said it refers to the new crescent, which shows itself once the sun has set. People in Makkah watched for that thin moon every month.
now: You step outside after sunset to take out the bins and there it is, a thin crescent above the rooftops. It came exactly when it should. {idea}The sky keeps its order without being asked.{/idea} Your days could use a little of that.
old: The moon is just there some nights and not others.
new: The moon keeps its turn behind the sun, and that order is a sign worth an oath.
try: Find out tonight's moon phase and look for it before you sleep.

title: The day lights everything up and shows it.
subtitle: Daylight that makes things visible

row.title: displayed
sub: the day shows things as they are

then: Mujahid said this means {idea}when the day illuminates{/idea}. He linked it to a matching oath in the next surah, by the day as it appears. The listeners knew the difference between a dark path and a lit one.
now: At night the messy room looks fine. Then the morning sun hits it and you see every cup and pile. {idea}Light does not create the mess, it shows it.{/idea} The same goes for the habits you only notice when someone points them out.
old: If no one sees it, it is not really a problem.
new: Things are already what they are; the light only shows them.
try: Pick one corner of your home and tidy it in daylight today.

title: Then the night comes and covers it all.
subtitle: The dark that takes over the sun's place
then: Ibn Kathir says the night {idea}covers the sun{/idea} when it disappears and the horizons go dark. The surah introduction notes that day and night are opposites in effect, {idea}just as good and evil are{/idea}.
now: It is late, the lights are off, and the house is quiet. This is when the small temptations get louder: the scrolling, the tab you would close if someone walked in. {trap}Darkness makes things feel like they do not count.{/trap} They still count.
old: Night is when nothing much happens.
new: Day and night are opposites, and so are the choices I make in each.
try: Set one rule for your phone after dark tonight and keep it once.

title: The sky, and the One who built it.
subtitle: A built roof points to its builder
then: Qatadah read this as {idea}the sky and its construction{/idea}; Mujahid as the sky and its Constructor. Ibn Kathir says both views connect, since building means raising. He cites the verse: with strength did We construct the heaven.
now: You lie on the grass at a picnic and look straight up. No pillars, no cracks, no repair crew. {idea}Something that big and that steady was built.{/idea} You would never assume a house built itself.
old: The sky is just empty space above me.
new: The sky is a building, and a building tells you someone built it.
try: Look up at the sky for one full minute today and say SubhanAllah.

title: The earth, and the One who spread it out.
subtitle: Ground laid flat so life can stand on it
then: Most early scholars, Mujahid, Qatadah and others, said this means {idea}He spread it out{/idea}. Ibn Abbas also said it means what He created in it, and that He proportioned it. Ibn Kathir pairs it with: We spread out the earth, how excellent a spreader.
now: You walk barefoot across the kitchen floor or a beach. The ground holds you without a thought. {reward}You have never once had to ask it to stay still.{/reward} Steadiness you never noticed is still a gift.
old: The ground is just the ground.
new: The earth was spread for me to stand on, and that is worth noticing.
try: Stand still outside for a moment today and feel the ground under you.

title: Your soul was shaped well, from the start.
subtitle: The self made sound on a natural way
then: After sky and earth, the oath turns to {idea}the soul itself{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says Allah created it sound and well-proportioned upon the Fitrah. He cites the hadith: {reward}every child is born upon the Fitrah{/reward}.
now: You hold a newborn at a family visit and nobody doubts that this child is good. You were that child once. {reward}The good in you is the original, not the add-on.{/reward} The mess came later and can be cleaned.
old: Deep down I am just a bad person.
new: My soul was made sound; what went wrong came after and is not who I am.
try: Write one good instinct you had as a child that you still have.

title: You already know right from wrong inside.
subtitle: Both paths were shown to the soul
then: Ibn Abbas said Allah {idea}explained the good and the evil to it{/idea}. Ibn Zayd said He placed both inside it. The surah introduction adds that this inner sense is real but not enough alone, which is why messengers were sent.
now: You are about to send the sharp reply in the work chat and something in your chest says don't. You know that voice. {idea}It was put there on purpose.{/idea} {trap}Arguing it down is the real choice.{/trap}
old: Right and wrong are just what each person decides.
new: The knowing was placed in me; my job is to listen to it.
try: Next time you feel that inner check today, stop and follow it once.

title: All those oaths were for this: purify the soul.
subtitle: Success is cleaning the self
then: Sun, moon, day, night, sky, earth, soul: all sworn by, and this is {idea}the answer{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says whoever purifies himself by obedience to Allah succeeds. Qatadah said it means {reward}cleansing it from low and ugly traits{/reward}.
now: Your feed is full of success: promotions, new cars, wedding photos. None of it shows the person who finally stopped lying to their spouse. {reward}That is the success this verse means.{/reward}
old: Success is what I can show people.
new: Success is the slow work of cleaning my own soul.
try: Pick one small ugly habit and skip it for one day.

title: Failure is burying the good inside you.
subtitle: Hiding the soul under corruption
then: The word here means to {trap}bury it{/trap}, to cover over what is good. Ibn Kathir sets it against the verse before: one person cleans the soul, the other hides it. {idea}Same soul, same inspiration, opposite results.{/idea}
now: Nobody wakes up and decides to become cold. It is one skipped prayer, one unkind joke laughed along with, one lie that worked. {trap}Layer by layer, the good gets buried.{/trap} {idea}It is still under there.{/idea}
old: I am fine, I just do a few things I should not.
new: Each small thing I let pile up is soil over the good in me.
try: Name one layer you have been piling on. Do the opposite of it once today.

title: Thamud said no because of their arrogance.
subtitle: The example of a people who buried the soul
then: Now the surah gives a real example. Mujahid and Qatadah said Thamud rejected their messenger because of {trap}the injustice and transgression they practised{/trap}. Their behaviour came first; {trap}the denial grew out of it{/trap}.
now: You know the truth about something but accepting it would mean changing how you live. So you find reasons to doubt it. {trap}The doubt is not about evidence, it is about comfort.{/trap} Notice when you do that.
old: I would accept it if the proof were stronger.
new: Sometimes I reject a truth because of how I live, not because of what I know.
try: Name one truth you keep arguing with. Ask what it would cost you to accept it.

title: Their most wretched man stepped forward.
subtitle: One man acts, a whole tribe stands behind
then: Ibn Kathir names him {trap}Qudar bin Salif{/trap}, the one who killed the she-camel. He was a strong, respected leader of noble lineage. The Prophet ﷺ described him in a sermon as {trap}a mighty man, invincible among his tribe{/trap}.
now: The loudest person in the office, the one everyone defers to, proposes something you know is wrong. Nobody says anything because of who he is. {trap}Rank does not make him right.{/trap} Your silence is still your choice.
old: If someone that important does it, it must be fine.
new: The most respected person in the room can still be the most wretched.
try: Think of one person you follow without question. Check one of their opinions yourself.

title: Salih warned them: leave Allah's camel and her water.
subtitle: A clear, simple limit they were given
then: The messenger was {idea}Salih{/idea}. He told them not to touch the she-camel of Allah with harm, and {idea}not to transgress in her drinking{/idea}. She had a day to drink and they had a day, as they all knew.
now: The rule is simple: one evening a week the phone stays off for the family. Everyone agreed. Then a message comes in and it feels small to break it. {trap}Small limits are where respect is tested.{/trap}
old: It is a minor rule, crossing it will not matter.
new: A clear limit from Allah is a test of respect, however small it looks.
try: Keep one small promise today exactly as you made it.

title: One man did it, but all of them agreed.
subtitle: Shared approval makes shared guilt
then: Qatadah said the leader {trap}did not kill the she-camel until their youth, elderly, men and women all pledged to him{/trap}. Because they cooperated, the punishment fell on them all. That is the meaning of made it equal.
now: Someone in the family group chat posts a cruel joke about a relative. You did not write it. You sent a laughing emoji. {trap}Approval is a kind of signature.{/trap} {idea}Staying out of it is also a choice.{/idea}
old: I did not do it, I just went along.
new: Going along with a wrong makes it partly mine.
try: Next time a group mocks someone, do not react with approval. Stay quiet, or speak up kindly.

title: Allah does not fear what comes after.
subtitle: No one can call Him to account
then: Ibn Abbas said: {idea}Allah does not fear any consequences from anyone{/idea}. Mujahid, Al-Hasan and others said the same. Rulers on earth worry about revenge and alliances. {idea}Allah has no such worry.{/idea}
now: You hold back from doing right because of what people might say or do: the boss, the in-laws, the comments section. {idea}Their reaction is not the final word.{/idea} {reward}The One you answer to is not afraid of any of them.{/reward}
old: I have to weigh what everyone will think before I act.
new: Only Allah's judgment is final, and He fears no one's reaction.
try: Do one right thing today that you have delayed out of fear of what people think.
